result.title: Learning to Compose: Recursive Self-Improvement of Shared Executable Stacks for Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
result.summary: Individually competent robot skills can fail when composed: tools may lack a required capability, completion signals may misrepresent physical progress, and one skill may leave a state that violates its successor's prerequisites. We introduce Recursia, a recursive self-improvement framework that treats the shared executable stack, rather than individual task programs, as the persistent unit of improvement. The stack integrates tools, skills with execution contracts, handoffs, and verifiers. Source-side execution traces guide failure attribution and the generation of missing tools or repairs to existing shared components. Generality checks, mechanism tests, and paired selection and regression gates determine which changes become the next parent. The resulting stack is frozen and reused through declarative task adapters, allowing source-derived changes to support new compositions without target-side code repair. Experiments cover LIBERO-Pro Long simulation and a physical Franka FR3 equipped with a Franka Hand. In simulation, Recursia improves success over ASPIRE by 5.8 percentage points under Pos perturbations and 15.1 points under Task perturbations. Across three physical compositional target tasks, it improves mean success over the Skill Document Only baseline by 40 percentage points. Analyses of constituent execution, candidate rejection, and inference drivers distinguish local mechanism improvements from complete task success and characterize the cost of feedback-conditioned orchestration. These results examine shared executable interfaces as a concrete mechanism for compositional transfer in robot programming.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Recursia，把共享可执行栈（工具、带执行契约的技能、交接、验证器）而非单个任务程序作为持续改进单元，用源侧执行轨迹做失败归因、生成缺失工具或修复，并以泛化检查、回归门选择下一代父代，冻结后经声明式任务适配器复用于新组合；在 LIBERO-Pro Long 仿真与 Franka FR3 真机上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于完成信号失真、技能交接的前置状态违反与验证器的表述，可能启发 LVR 中「证据是否支持当前推理状态、何时停止」的问题表述，可供核查；但对象为机器人技能组合，与多模态 latent 推理相距较远。
